subject: Dedicated capacity sizing call - follow up and scheduling
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing call - next steps

Hi Sam —

Great to meet earlier today — appreciate you walking us through the payment-processing flows and the current integration. Quick recap from our side:

- Primary workloads: fraud-scoring model + customer support assistant (prompted generation for responses).
- Peak traffic window: US business hours, Monday–Friday.
- Current production QPS estimate (burst): ~220 req/s, steady-state ~80 req/s.
- Typical context length: 512 tokens input, ~150 tokens generated on average.
- Target latency: p95 < 250ms for the customer-facing assistant, p95 < 500ms acceptable for async fraud scoring.

Next step: schedule a 45-minute dedicated capacity sizing call with our solutions engineering lead to align on throughput, latency SLOs, batching strategy, and any hardware constraints.

Proposed agenda:
1) Confirm traffic patterns and peak concurrency
2) Review p95 and p99 latency targets by route
3) Map model variants (quantization/replicas) to expected cost/latency
4) Identify data isolation and security requirements for Dedicated

Can you share 2–3 windows that work next week? I've included Neha (solutions) on cc. If helpful, here is my Calendly: https://calendly.com/marissa-redwood/dedicated-sizing-30m

Also attaching a short capacity sizing template — a quick fill of current qps, avg tokens, and burst patterns will let us run a first-cut sizing before the call.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Marissa —

Thanks for the recap and the template. That matches what we discussed. High-level answers below (I can get more detail into the spreadsheet before the call):

- Steady QPS: 70–90 req/s
- Burst (promo days / morning spikes): up to 240 req/s for short periods (2–10 minutes)
- Avg tokens: ~650 total (input + output), input is usually ~500, output ~150
- Concurrency: typical concurrent users ~150, can spike to ~400
- SLOs: customer chat p95 <= 250ms; fraud scoring p95 <= 450ms (batchable)

Available windows next week:
- Tue 2026-01-20 10:00–11:00 PT
- Wed 2026-01-21 13:00–14:00 PT
- Thu 2026-01-22 09:00–10:00 PT

Please loop in any infra folks who'd need to be on the sizing call. We'll try to pre-fill the template by Monday.
